schema_notes: level_m = deck surface height above design waterline (negative = below). Positions: bow/mid/stern + port/starboard/centre. confidence: sourced = stated by a cited source; typical = standard for this ship type/period, not verified this session; reconstruction = game simplification.

basis.fact: Standard displacement 15,140 t; length 122 m (museum figure, between perpendiculars); width 23.2 m; speed 18 kt; main armament 12-inch x4 (2 twin mounts), secondary 6-inch x14
Overall length 131.7 m (432 ft), beam 23.2 m, normal draught ~8.3 m, 15,140 long tons normal load, crew about 830
Crew figure 860 appears in the museum leaflet (snippet truncated)
25 Belleville boilers, 2 vertical triple-expansion engines, 2 shafts, 15,000 ihp
Armour: belt 229-102 mm, casemates 152-51 mm, deck 76-51 mm (Harvey nickel per Navypedia; other sources say Krupp cemented)
Main guns 40-cal 30.5 cm twin mounts, one fore and one aft; 8 cm guns on the upper deck, 10 per side
Upper deck is wooden planking; it sounds underfoot

On the open top bridge (最上艦橋) the floor marks where Togo stood (front row, right of centre) with Chief of Staff Kato Tomosaburo and staff officer Akiyama Saneyuki behind him; chart room and conning tower adjoin
Togo stood on the compass deck above the bridge; Z flag hoisted at about 13:55 on 27 May 1905
Hit 32 times at Tsushima, 8 dead (one account; others say 40+ hits)
On 11 Sep 1905 the aft magazine exploded while she was moored in Sasebo harbour and she sank in shallow water
Death toll from the Sasebo explosion: 339 or 251 depending on source; contemporary press said ~600
Refloated 8 Aug 1906; repairs took over two years
Primary record: 明治三十八年 軍艦三笠罹災関係 held by the NIDS library
As a memorial ship, everything below the lower deck is filled with concrete and earth (Washington Treaty); the main guns are replicas
The museum restored the captain's cabin and the guns; exhibits about the Battle of the Japan Sea are inside
The museum tour map lists the conning tower, main armament, 6-inch auxiliary guns, bower anchor and bow crest

rising-sun naval ensign at the stern

lighting.type: electric incandescent lamps with steam dynamos, oil lamps as backup, searchlights on bridges and masts
lighting.mood: dim yellow interior; bright overcast daylight on the deck (the Tsushima battle day was foggy with high waves)

props_period: 白い第二種軍装 vs 紺の第一種軍装 (May = dark winter uniforms)

flooding.watertight_subdivision: Steel hull with transverse watertight bulkheads, a double bottom under the machinery, and side coal bunkers acting as protective compartments. The compartment count is unverified.
flooding.bulkhead_confidence: reconstruction (positions inferred from the turret and funnel layout)
flooding.pumps: Steam-driven main circulating and bilge pumps in the machinery spaces, plus hand pumps (typical)
flooding.sea_cocks: Magazine flooding cocks (弾火薬庫注水弁) next to each magazine (standard practice; the 1905 accident shows the risk). Kingston valves for the condensers.

magazines.name: 6-inch and 8 cm
magazines.position: distributed along the battery, below the waterline

sequence: Hit ~32-40 times, mostly in the upper works
Fire started near the aft magazine at night (cause disputed; one theory is sailors drinking alcohol lit by flame)
Aft magazine detonated, blowing out the hull aft
Sank by the stern in shallow harbour water; settled on the bottom with superstructure and masts above water (period photos)
Refloated 8 Aug 1906 and repaired for 2+ years

game_sinking_hooks: Fire in the aft handling room: a timer to the magazine explosion unless the flood cocks are opened
Opening the magazine flood cocks floods the aft compartments, giving a stern trim
The Sasebo harbour scenario: the ship settles upright on the bottom rather than capsizing (shallow water)

uncertain: Exact deck heights and room dimensions are estimates; the museum ship below the lower deck is filled with concrete, so no physical evidence of the lower spaces exists today.
Belt armour type (Harvey vs Krupp) is disputed between sources.
Exact positions of the cabins (長官公室 etc.) follow RN practice and need checking against the museum floor plan (official site unreachable this session).
Official museum pages (kinenkan-mikasa.or.jp) could not be fetched; facts come from search-result snippets.
